TS0330001.solution: Choose a different id or --out, or pass --force to overwrite.

TS0330002.message: The workspace already holds a demo resource at {path}.
TS0330002.solution: Use a different workspace with -w, or pass --force to overwrite the demo files there.

TS0330003.solution: Check that the directory exists, is writable, and that no plain file is sitting where a directory is needed. Demo files this run wrote were removed and any it overwrote were put back, though empty directories it created can remain.

TS0330004.message: Could not read the workspace at {path}: {reason}
TS0330004.solution: Check that the workspace directory and every directory and *.tap.yml file under it can be read, then run `tapstate up` again.

TS0330005.message: The workspace at {path} holds no pipeline (a *.tap.yml with kind: pipeline), so there is nothing to bring up.
TS0330005.solution: Run `tapstate new` to write one, or point -w at a workspace that holds a pipeline.

TS0330006.message: `{path}` already exists and is not the tapstate shortcut.
TS0330006.solution: Leave it in place - tapstate works without the shortcut. Remove that file yourself if you want the `tap` name, then run `tapstate alias install` again.

TS0330007.solution: Run this where tapstate is installed, or set TAPSTATE_INSTALL_DIR to that directory - the same variable the installer honours.

TS0330008.message: The `tap` shortcut at `{path}` could not be created or removed: {reason}
TS0330008.solution: Check that the directory exists and you can write to it, then run `tapstate alias install` again. tapstate itself works without the shortcut.

TS0330009.message: The local development stack cannot be run in Docker: {reason}.
TS0330009.solution: Install Docker with the Compose v2 plugin and make sure it is running, then run `tapstate up` again - or point the workspace at a server you already run with --server.

TS0330010.message: This workspace is not bound to a server, and there is nothing to ask.
TS0330010.solution: Pass --server <url> to name the server to use, or --start-local to start the local development stack on {server}.

TS0330011.message: Signing in to {server} needs a password, and there is nothing to ask.
TS0330011.solution: Set {variable} in the environment, or pass --server for a server you are already signed in to.

TS0330012.message: Signing in to {server} did not return a usable persistent session.
TS0330012.solution: Check the server connection and compatibility, then run `tapstate up` again.

TS0330013.solution: Pick a connector id from the catalog; run `tapstate new` interactively to choose one.

TS0330014.message: This release installs these connectors: {official}. '{connector}' is in the catalog but is not one of them.
TS0330014.solution: Pick one of the connectors listed above. The supported set grows as connectors complete certification, so a connector missing here is not necessarily faulty.

TS0330015.message: Could not download the published connector '{connector}': {reason}
TS0330015.solution: Check network access to GitHub Releases, or set TAPSTATE_CONNECTORS_URL to an HTTPS mirror that carries the connector assets, then retry. You can still register a local jar path.

TS0330016.message: Artifact {path} declares kind '{kind}' but sits in a '{dir}' directory.
TS0330016.solution: Move it under a '{kind}' directory, or change its declared kind to match.

TS0330017.message: No resource with id '{id}' in the workspace.
TS0330017.solution: Run `tapstate ls` to see the available resources.

TS0330018.message: Could not reach any Tapstate server among the seeds: {seeds}.
TS0330018.solution: Check the addresses are correct and that a Tapstate server is running there, then try connect again.

TS0330019.message: The request to {server} timed out before the server answered.
TS0330019.solution: The server may be busy or the upload large. It may have completed there anyway — re-running a register is safe (it is idempotent). Wait and retry, or check the server logs.

TS0330020.message: The `{verb}` command needs a connection to a Tapstate server.

TS0330021.message: The `{verb}` command needs you to sign in first.

TS0330022.message: The `{verb}` command is reserved but not implemented yet.
TS0330022.solution: Use the commands it will be built from in the meantime; `help` lists what this build can do.

TS0330023.message: `{verb}` works inside the Tapstate session, not as a one-shot command.
TS0330023.solution: Start `tapstate` with no arguments and type `{verb}` at the prompt; `help` lists the session commands.

TS0330024.solution: Install the complete Tapstate CLI bundle, including libexec/tapstate-mcp, and retry.

TS0330025.message: `watch` redraws one row in place, which needs a terminal; here its output is a pipe or a file.
TS0330025.solution: Use `tail <source>.<collection>` for a stream you can pipe, or `<source>.<collection>.find(...)` for a one-shot look.

TS0330026.message: `{verb}` clears what the pipeline accumulated, and there is no terminal here to confirm at.
TS0330026.solution: Add `-y` to go ahead without being asked, or run `stop <pipeline-id> --keep-state` to stop it and keep everything it has.

TS0330027.message: `--if-match` names one version, but this apply covers {count} resources.
TS0330027.solution: Apply the single file you are editing, or drop `--if-match` and let the batch apply unconditionally.

TS0330028.message: {pipeline} was left as it is: {count} start check question(s) need an answer, and there is no terminal here to ask at.
TS0330028.solution: Answer them on the command line: {commands}

TS0330029.message: This server does not run start checks, so {option} cannot take effect; nothing was started.
TS0330029.solution: Upgrade the server, or start without {option}.

TS0330030.message: The server started {pipeline} without running start checks; it is likely older than this client.
TS0330030.solution: The pipeline was started; inspect its status. Upgrade the server before relying on start checks for future starts.

TS0330031.message: --decide {decide} is not an answer: write <check>=<action>, or <check>/<subject>=<action> for one question.

TS0330032.message: --decide {decide} cannot be taken: {findings} do(es) not offer that answer.
TS0330032.solution: Answer each of them on its own with --decide <check>/<subject>=<action>, using an answer it offers.

TS0330033.message: --decide {decide} answers a start check that refuses the start, and no answer changes a refusal.
TS0330033.solution: Read the start checks for what the refusal needs changed, change it, then start again.

TS0330034.message: The start of {pipeline} was sent to {server}, and no answer came back in time; it may have gone ahead there.
TS0330034.solution: Check with 'tapstate status {pipeline}' before starting it again.

TS0330035.message: The context configuration at `{path}` is unsafe or invalid: {reason}
TS0330035.solution: Fix or remove the configuration file, then run the context manager again. The invalid file was not overwritten.

TS0330036.message: The context configuration at `{path}` uses unsupported schema version `{version}`.
TS0330036.solution: Use a compatible tapstate release or migrate the configuration with a release that supports this version.

TS0330037.message: The context configuration path `{path}` is not owner-only: {reason}
TS0330037.solution: Restore ownership and owner-only permissions, then retry. Tapstate will not read or overwrite an unsafe file.

TS0330038.message: The auth cache at `{path}` is unsafe or invalid: {reason}
TS0330038.solution: Sign in again after checking the context target. The invalid auth file was not overwritten.

TS0330039.message: The auth cache at `{path}` uses unsupported schema version `{version}`.
TS0330039.solution: Use a compatible tapstate release or sign in again with this release.

TS0330040.message: The auth cache path `{path}` is not owner-only: {reason}
TS0330040.solution: Restore ownership and owner-only permissions, then retry. Tapstate will not read or overwrite an unsafe auth file.

TS0330041.message: The cached session for `{principal}` was rejected by the server: {code}.
TS0330041.solution: Run `tapstate auth login` again for this context.

TS0330042.message: The cached session for `{principal}` could not be exchanged because the server was unreachable.
TS0330042.solution: Check the server connection and retry, or run `tapstate auth login` again.

TS0330043.message: Login for context `{context}` did not return a usable persistent session.
TS0330043.solution: Check the server connection and compatibility, then run `tapstate auth login` again.

TS0330044.message: Login for `{principal}` was rejected by the server: {code}.
TS0330044.solution: Check the username and password, then run `tapstate auth login` again.

TS0330045.message: The remote session for context `{context}` could not be revoked; the local cache was kept.
TS0330045.solution: Retry when the server is reachable, or use `tapstate auth logout --local-only` to remove only the local cache.

TS0330046.message: The session for context `{context}` changed while logout was in progress; the newer local session was kept.
TS0330046.solution: Run `tapstate auth status` to inspect the current session, then retry logout if needed.

TS0330047.solution: Read storage or configuration help and provide request secrets only in a local JSON file.

TS0330048.solution: Use `tapstate auth login [username]`, `tapstate auth status`, or `tapstate auth logout [--local-only]`.

TS0330049.solution: Run `tapstate context` in an interactive terminal and choose one of the offered actions.

TS0330050.solution: Use a non-empty name, at least one absolute HTTP(S) seed, and valid context settings.

TS0330051.solution: Open the context manager and choose an existing context or create this one.

TS0330052.solution: Edit the existing context or choose another name.

TS0330053.message: `--connect` and `--context` select different kinds of target and cannot be used together.
TS0330053.solution: Keep `--connect` for a temporary target, or keep `--context` for a saved context.

TS0330054.message: The `{verb}` command needs a server context, but no target was selected.
TS0330054.solution: Use `--context`, set `TAPSTATE_CONTEXT`, bind this exact workspace, or use `--connect` for a temporary target.

TS0330055.message: Server seed {seed} uses plaintext HTTP outside loopback.
TS0330055.solution: Use HTTPS for remote servers; HTTP is allowed only for a loopback development server.

TS0330056.message: Server seed {seed} did not return its anonymous cluster identity.
TS0330056.solution: Check that the seed is reachable and serves /.well-known/tapstate, then try again.

TS0330057.message: Server seed {seed} returned an invalid cluster identity ({reason}).
TS0330057.solution: Check that the URL targets a compatible Tapstate server and has not been replaced by another service.

TS0330058.message: Server seed {seed} refused anonymous issuer discovery: {reason}
TS0330058.solution: A server older than this CLI does not serve /.well-known/tapstate; upgrade the server, or use a CLI matching its version.

TS0330059.message: Server seed {seed} reports issuer {actual}, but {expected} was required.
TS0330059.solution: Check the context seeds and sign in again only after confirming that this is the intended cluster.

TS0330060.message: This CLI is {cli} and the server it connected to is {server}.
TS0330060.solution: Install the CLI that matches the server, or connect to a server on {cli}; where the two disagree, the server decides.

TS0330061.message: The result of the request to {server} could not be confirmed.
TS0330061.solution: Check the current resource state before retrying a write. Restore connectivity if needed; the server may have completed the request.

TS0330062.message: Connection lost: no reachable cluster member.
TS0330062.solution: Restore connectivity, then reconnect. The last request result may be unconfirmed; check the current resource state before retrying a write.

TS0330063.message: The stream stopped after {attempts} consecutive attachments ended without a frame.
TS0330063.solution: Check the stream endpoint and network path, then reconnect. This does not establish whether the pipeline is running or failed.
